newsitem.title: FRANCE: Juppe to freeze 1998 spending at current levels.
newsitem.headline: Juppe to freeze 1998 spending at current levels.

text.p: French Prime Minister Alain Juppe plans to freeze spending at current levels in the 1998 budget, afternoon daily Le Monde said on Monday.

"The spending framework for 1998, to be sent soon to all government members, will hold spending at last year's levels. State spending of 1,563 billion francs will be carried over in current francs," the newspaper said. This means for the second straight year, spending will fall by the amount of inflation, it said.
The newspaper also said Juppe plans no new deep tax cuts.
"Given the narrow budgetary margin, the cut (in taxes) should be limited to 12.5 billion francs in 1998.
The newspaper said that the letters to ministers outlining spending plans were meant to symbolize that "budgetary rigor will be maintained but not increased".

Le Monde, citing unnamed sources close to the prime minister, said Juppe would not pledge additional reductions in income taxes. And because he had so little room for manoeuvre, he would have to limit to 12.5 billion francs the income tax cuts that could take place in 1998, the newspaper said.
In addition, even if social security deficits were to increase, the prime minister has no plan under consideration to correct such a situation at this time, Le Monde said.
